trainers.instruction: This is a map of North Africa. Drag the boat along the Nile.

atoms.b: At 6,700 kilometres long, the Nile is the longest ((++river road)) in Africa and one of the longest in the world. The river has two main sources, but the longest route starts in Lake Victoria and flows ((++north east)) until it reaches the Mediterranean Sea.

Most major cities in Egypt have been ((++built destroyed)) along the banks of the Nile. From the ancient Egyptians to the present day, it has been crucial for transport, growing crops and providing drinking water.
The Nile is also home to a wide variety of animal species. The most famous of these is the Nile crocodile, which is one of the largest ((++reptiles mammals)) in the world.

hint.label: Did you know?
text: The Atlas Mountains are named after the Greek mythological figure: Atlas. He was forced to hold up the heavens for eternity and was later turned to stone — supposedly forming this mountain range.

atoms.a: The Atlas Mountains are a mountain range in North Africa that stretch across 2,400 kilometres.
The mountains form a natural climate barrier, separating the Sahara Desert to the south from the Mediterranean to the north.
The Atlas Mountains are mainly inhabited by the indigenous Amazigh people, who live in mountain villages.
atoms.sound: The Atlas Mountains are mainly inhabited by the indigenous Amuhzeekh people, who live in mountain villages.

atoms.a: The region is home to the Barbary macaque, which is the only monkey in Africa found north of the Sahara Desert.
atoms.sound: The region is home to the Barberry mahkaak, which is the only monkey in Africa found north of the Sahara Desert.

atoms.b: This ancient ((++city field)), known as Leptis Magna, is one of the most impressive surviving ruins from the Roman Empire. It is located on the coast of Libya.
Its ruins were ((++excavated built)) in the 1920s by archaeologists, who were shocked that a huge amount of the city had been preserved, buried under the sand dunes.
Lots of the grand buildings still survive in part today. The remains of an amphitheatre, a ((++bathhouse supermarket)) and many arches can all clearly be made out.

hint.label: Amphitheatre
hint.text: An amphitheatre is a large, open-air venue used for performances.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

hint.label: Sahara Desert map
text: The Sahara desert covers the majority of northern Africa.

atoms.text: The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world. At a huge 9.2 million square kilometres, it covers most of North Africa and reaches up to 55 °C during the summer.
The only fertile areas, called oases, are infrequent and small. The most famous of these is the Siwa Oasis in Egypt, known for its salt lake, palm trees and ruins.
atoms.sound: The only fertile areas, called oases, are infrequent and small. The most famous of these is the Seewa Oasis in Egypt, known for its salt lake, palm trees and ruins.

atoms.text: Nomadic peoples, such as the Toubou and Bedouin, often use camels to get around and transport goods. Camels can go days without water because they store fat in their humps, which can be used for energy.
atoms.sound: Nomadic peoples, such as the Tooboo and Bedouin, often use camels to get around and transport goods. Camels can go days without water because they store fat in their humps, which can be used for energy.
